claims.text: The material under study is an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
Introducing a secondary phase with a different electrochemical potential enhances galvanic coupling between the primary and secondary phases.
Enhanced galvanic coupling increases the corrosion reaction.
Enhanced galvanic coupling increases the wear process.
The coupled increases in corrosion and wear accelerate total degradation.
At 600°C under simultaneous wear and corrosion, the secondary-phase alloy will exhibit 30% greater total degradation than the baseline.
At 600°C under simultaneous wear and corrosion, the secondary-phase alloy will exhibit a 25% higher corrosion rate than the baseline.
At 600°C under simultaneous wear and corrosion, the secondary-phase alloy will exhibit a 20% higher wear rate than the baseline.
The baseline is AlCoCrFeNi without the introduced secondary phase.
The proposed controlled comparison subjects alloys with and without the secondary phase to the same elevated-temperature simultaneous wear-corrosion exposure.
Failure of the secondary phase to produce significant increases in total degradation, corrosion rate, and wear rate would falsify the hypothesis.
